title: US proof, SMS, mint, and silver proof sets — silver content
unit: troy ounces ASW (actual silver weight) per set or coin as named

conventions.note: 90% set ASW uses standard 90% coin weights (dime 2.50 g, quarter 6.25 g, half 12.50 g at 90% fine), consistent with the site’s 0.7234 ozt per $1 face convention. 40% Kennedy half uses 11.50 g at 40%. 2019+ Silver Proof ASW uses U.S. Mint nominal weights at 0.999 fine.

sources.name: United States Mint
sources.what: Official Silver Proof Set specifications from 2019: dime 2.537 g, quarter 6.343 g, half dollar 12.685 g, 99.9% silver; annual set product pages (including the 2026 Silver Proof Set).

sources.name: PCGS
sources.what: Mint-set and proof-set composition, including 1968–1970 mint sets (single Denver 40% Kennedy half) and the 1970-D half as a mint-set-only issue; 40% Kennedy specifications.

sources.name: CoinWorld
sources.what: Reporting that 2019+ Silver Proof catalog wording about a lower specification-limit weight did not mean the Mint reduced silver content; official nominal weights still apply.

sources.name: CoinNews / CoinWeek-type references
sources.what: Year-by-year set contents used as a check, including the 2021 Silver Proof Set (two quarters) and published 2026 Silver Proof Set quarter count.

sources.name: Mint Set Guide / Proof Set Guide
sources.what: Secondary check of coins included in annual mint and proof sets (for example 1968–1970 10-coin mint sets with a single half dollar).

caveats: Figures are melt (ASW × live silver spot), not collector value or what a dealer will pay.
Years or products marked “varies” are left blank rather than guessed (1947–1958 double mint sets; Limited Edition Silver Proof Sets that add a Silver Eagle; packaging variants).
Regular proof sets for 1971–present, including 1980, are clad and have no silver. Silver Proof sets are a separate product starting in 1992.
1968–1970 mint sets contain one 40% Kennedy half (the Denver coin), not two. The 1969 mint set is 0.1479 ozt, not a pair of halves.
2012 Silver Proof Set uses the same 90% dime + five quarters + half makeup as other 2010–2018 sets (ASW 1.3383 ozt).
CPI and copper on the charts page are separate from this table.

sets.name: 1950 Proof Set
sets.silverCoins: 90% dime, quarter, and half ($0.85 face). Cent and nickel are not silver.
sets.note: Standard 5-coin proof set. Last 90% circulating-type proof set is 1964.

sets.name: 1950 Uncirculated Mint Set (double set)
sets.silverCoins: 90% dimes, quarters, and halves from each mint that struck them, typically two of each coin (double set packaging).
sets.note: 1947–1958 uncirculated sets were double sets: two of each coin from each issuing mint, so silver content depends on which mints struck dimes, quarters, and halves that year. Marked varies rather than assuming a single ASW.

The 2019 set also included a separately packaged 2019-W reverse-proof Lincoln cent and a Native American dollar; neither contains silver, and they are not added to ASW. Limited Edition Silver Proof Sets (which add a Silver Eagle) are a different product and are marked varies.

sets.name: 2026 Silver Proof Set
sets.silverCoins: .999 fine dime, five quarters, and half (Semiquincentennial / 1776–2026 designs), using the same Mint nominal weights as 2019+.
sets.note: 2026 Silver Proof Set is described as including five 99.9% silver quarters plus the silver dime and half. ASW uses the same official 2019+ nominal weights (1.5076 ozt). If a particular packaging variant adds or omits a silver coin, treat it as varies.

sets.name: 2026 Uncirculated Mint Set
sets.silverCoins: None in the regular uncirculated / mint set (clad or base-metal denominations, including clad Ike or SBA dollars where included).
sets.note: Regular uncirculated mint set has no silver. 40% Ikes (1971–74, 1976) and later silver products were sold separately.

sets.name: Limited Edition Silver Proof Set (various years)
sets.silverCoins: Standard Silver Proof silver coins plus a Proof Silver Eagle (and sometimes other extras). Contents and years of issue vary.
sets.note: Do not use the standard Silver Proof Set ASW for a Limited Edition set. The added American Silver Eagle changes the total; confirm the coins in the box rather than assuming a year.
